observations.seen: The stock brownstone street kit is reasonably detailed but unrelated to the arena: a flat plane dropped in front of a facade.
Character meshes and buildings are decent purchased or scanned assets. Lamp posts, signs, and arena borders are box primitives.
Building textures are acceptable. Character textures are erased by flat tint overrides, and the floor is untextured.
Everything has the same matte response. Brick, glass, asphalt, cloth, and skin are indistinguishable in sheen.
No visible specular, no roughness variation, and windows show no reflections. It reads like Lambert shading.
Flat, low-contrast fill with no key, no rim to separate fighters from the busy background, and a sourceless floor hotspot.
No cast shadows from fighters; foot decals stand in for them. No contact shadowing under the facade.
Uniform grey ambient with no AO and no grounding.
No visible environment reflections on glass, floor, or characters (inferred: likely no envmap or a dim one).
Murky mid-grey exposure. Blacks are lifted and highlights are weak, so nothing pops.
No obvious sRGB double-gamma errors, but the palette is desaturated mud apart from the UI-colored team tints.
Thin floor lines and railings show crawling and stair-stepping (partly inferred through JPEG).
No meaningful bloom on emissive signs or lines, no color grade, no DoF, no vignette.
Hit moments have no sparks, flashes, or trails beyond translucent smears.
A handful of tiny specks, invisible at gameplay scale.
Poses look like competent mocap (stance, kick, launch), but the smear/ghosting obscures them (inferred).
Fighters are small and monochrome-tinted, which makes them look like placeholders. Silhouettes get lost against the facade.
Wide, distant, high-ish framing. Orbiting the angle mid-fight hurts the 2D-plane readability that fighters depend on.
Subjects sit in the middle third, the foreground is wasted, the background is busy, and combo labels block the action.
Facade scale reads correctly, but the tiny crowd figurines break scale. No fog or value falloff for depth.
No fog, haze, volumetrics, rain, or steam, despite a night street that calls for them.
Team colors make P1 and P2 identifiable. Combo plates occlude hits and the smears confuse state.
The HUD cards are clean and consistent, but they sit outside the game and look like a web dashboard. Debug-style nav ("Evidence", "Deploy check", "npm") ships in production.
Bold condensed names and the tracked mono labels work. Small labels are low contrast.
No hitstop, shake, flash, or impact audio-visual feedback is visible. Floating text clips into characters.
Portrait stack with tiny fighters, a black void in a third of the canvas, keyboard hints instead of touch controls, and cropped buttons.
An early-2010s tech-demo feel wrapped in a polished web shell.
Rich-looking arcade backdrop, but it appears to be flat plates with no parallax or integration; bottom third is a void.
Visible 3D geometry is rounded-rect blocks, line tubes, and a box pedestal; everything else reads as imagery.
Backdrop plates are detailed; the blocks are untextured, and the grid backplane is flat color.
The jelly/candy block shader with specular and subsurface-ish glow is the strongest element; nothing else has material definition.
Blocks sell "glossy plastic" but don't pick up neighbor emissives; the frame and pedestal read as unlit flat.
Lighting is neon-flavored, but light doesn't visibly fall onto the well, floor or blocks from the tubes.
No visible cast or contact shadows anywhere; blocks float on the grid plane.
No AO between blocks or at well edges; the ambient is flat navy.
Block highlights suggest an env map, but there is no floor or frame reflection where neon begs for it.
Saturated without clipping mush; highlights roll off acceptably and nothing is washed out.
Coherent cyan/magenta/orange palette, though the block rainbow fights the cyan grid.
Edges look clean at capture scale; thin 1px grid and tube lines are likely to shimmer in motion.
Moderate bloom on tubes, tasteful rather than hazy; no DoF, chromatic or grade work selling depth.
One orange ring in one frame; no lock, drop or clear effects visible elsewhere.
A handful of embers around the ring; otherwise none.
The mascot pose and environment are identical across all three frames, with no visible secondary motion.
The mascot art is appealing, but it's an unlit sticker on a hard-edged rectangle, disconnected from the scene.
Locked, dead-on, flat framing that throws away all depth; identical across states.
Symmetric and centered with a clear focal point, but large dead zones low and the marquee clipped by the HUD.
No perspective cues, fog layering or parallax; the backdrop reads as a wall 1m behind the grid.
No haze, volumetric light or dust; the only atmosphere is the bloom halo.
Block colors are distinct, but the ghost piece is low-contrast dark gray, heavy gridlines compete with pieces, and the center hotspot sits behind play.
Clean dark cards, but tiny text at 1080p, the debug-looking button bar on desktop, and the mobile Next panel occluding the board.
Legible sans with consistent weights, but undersized labels and generic system-UI feel with no arcade identity.
No visible feedback between frames: no shake, flash, squash or score pop.
The board fills the width, but the HUD overlaps play, the world is cut away, and the button bar is oversized and generic.
Nice block shader and attractive backdrop art can't hide a static, flat, unshadowed 2D presentation.
The backdrop is gorgeous (8+ in isolation), but it's a static plate. The authored 3D world is six platforms, one flat slab, and a white plane.
Ice platforms are decent stylized low-poly. The tree slab is primitive cones on a box, the coins are bare ellipsoids, the grey bars look like debug geometry, and the octahedron is a stock primitive.
Platforms have some painted color variation. The slab, coins, bars, and ground are flat colors with no texture.
Emissive rim on platforms works. Everything else reads as unlit flat or basic Lambert with no roughness or spec variation.
No visible specular response, fresnel, or roughness differentiation anywhere in the 3D layer. Ice and snow should sell this and don't.
Lighting is baked into the backdrop. The 3D layer gets flat ambient-plus-emissive with no key-light direction matching the painting's moonlight or lantern warmth.
No visible cast shadows from the character, platforms, or slab, and no contact shadows. Objects float with no grounding.
The blue ambient matches the palette, but it's uniform with no AO or occlusion in crevices or under platforms.
No visible reflections or environment response on ice, snow, or crystal.
The octahedron and dash slash clip to pure white. The ground is blown out. Midtones are fine because the backdrop is pre-graded.
The palette is cohesive (blue plus warm accents). The pink octahedron and olive coins clash, and the 3D layer is slightly desaturated against the plate.
Desktop edges are acceptable. Mobile is visibly soft or blurry, consistent with a low render scale.
Bloom is the only visible pass, and it's overdriven: haze around pickups and on mobile. No DOF, color grade, or vignette tied to gameplay.
The dash slash and relay ring exist but are a single flat card and a ring. No trails, sparks, snow kick-up, or layered effects.
No falling snow, breath, sparkle on pickups, or dash particles. In a snow level that is a glaring omission.
Identical pose across three frames suggests a sprite or single pose. No squash, lean, or secondary motion on the scarf is visible.
The design is appealing and on-style. It's small, has no rim light against the busy backdrop, and gets occluded by the pickup.
Static side-on framing with almost no movement between frames. The 3D projection doesn't match the backdrop's implied perspective (the slab is viewed from above).
The play path sits in a narrow mid band. The top-center is dominated by an ugly slab, and the bottom 15% is empty white.
3D and 2D layers don't share a horizon or scale. Platforms float with no depth cues, shadows, or parallax.
All atmosphere is painted. No real-time fog, snowfall, or light shafts bridge the 3D and 2D layers.
The platform path is readable. Coins are near-invisible dark blobs, the grey bars are ambiguous, the pickup hides the player, and Lives 0 during play is confusing.
The HUD is clean, consistent, and glassy. The keybind legend is microscopic, and the HUD is generic web-dashboard rather than game-styled.
The type is legible, the hierarchy is OK, and it's on-palette. The legend text is unreadable and there is truncation on mobile.
No feedback is visible: no hit-stop, screen shake, particles, coin pop, or trail. Frames 03 and 04 are nearly identical.
The play band is tiny, about 50% of the screen is HUD and controls, the image is blurry, the character is lost, and data is truncated or missing.
One excellent painted plate masks a prototype-grade 3D layer. Strip the backdrop and this is a 2–3.
Flat-shaded plane world, sparse primitive trees, two stands, empty sky.
The car silhouette is decent but faceted. Environment pieces are boxes, slabs and spheres.
Effectively no textures: asphalt, grass, sand and seats are all flat color.
Car has some gloss. Everything else is matte flat albedo with no roughness variation.
Car spec is plausible but clips. Asphalt has no micro-roughness or wetness, so nothing reads as a real material.
Single soft key with no strong directional sun read and no light shaping. Scenes look flatly lit.
Faint car contact shadow. Stands, trees and gantry cast nothing visible onto the ground.
Ambient is uniform grey with no AO grounding in crevices, wheels or stand bases.
Car shows weak env response. No sky reflection on car paint, no ground reflections.
Filmic-ish rolloff in the sky, but highlights clip (wing, gantry) and midtones are grey-washed.
Coherent pastel sunset palette but desaturated, with grey haze crushing contrast.
Edges are mostly clean at 1080p. Some stair-stepping on thin kerbs and distant poles.
Bloom on lane strips and vignette only. The bloom is smeary and the haze lowers contrast.
One glow puff and placeholder drift ring. No smoke, sparks or speed effects.
Effectively no particle tire smoke. Skid marks are disc or rectangle decals.
No visible wheel steer angle, body roll or suspension cues in stills.
The car is the most authored asset and reads as an F1-ish racer, but it is low-poly and lacks livery detail.
Desktop chase height is OK in the opening, but mid and action shots are too close and too tilted. Mobile is far too close.
Lower half of the frame is empty grey asphalt, and the horizon is cluttered with tiny props.
Untextured ground gives no speed or scale cues. 177 km/h reads as stationary.
Distance haze exists but behaves like a grey wash, not aerial perspective. No sky detail.
Track edges are readable via kerbs and lines, but overlapping slabs confuse the racing line.
Clean glassy panels with good hierarchy. The stats cluster is dense, and "GGhost OFF" is a label bug.
Crisp sans-serif with good weight contrast. Micro-labels are too small on desktop.
No screen shake, FOV kick, motion blur, smoke or speed lines. Feels static.
Car is cropped, the forward view is minimal, HUD and controls eat about 25%, and debug-looking ellipse dominates.
Reads as a programmer-art prototype with a nice HUD on top.
Single straight lane on an infinite flat green plane, with ellipsoid blobs as hills and trees; no world identity beyond a box "castle".
Almost everything is primitives (boxes, bevel boxes, ellipsoids, cylinders); crates and barrels are the only authored-looking props.
Flat vertex colors everywhere; only the crates and barrels carry textures, and they clash stylistically.
Uniform matte plastic; grass, wood, stone and ball are indistinguishable in response.
No roughness or metal variation and no specular cues; the ball has no highlight worth mentioning.
Clean single sun with decent key/fill balance, but no time-of-day mood, no rim light and no light accents at the goal.
Soft shadows present and stable; contact shadows under props are weak, and fence shadows band and stretch in the wide shot.
Flat hemispheric fill with no visible AO, so objects float and box seams don't darken.
No visible environment reflections on the ball, crates or anything else.
No clipping and a pleasant pastel range on desktop; slightly flat. Mobile is visibly washed.
Coherent palette, but salmon-orange obstacles and signs compete with the goal and the teal/green clash is muddy.
Edges are clean at desktop resolution, with mild shimmer likely on thin fence rails (inferred).
Bloom on the target ring is the only visible pass; no AO, color grade or vignette, and the mobile softness looks unintended.
Emissive ring and beam plus a ring decal at the ball; no impact, sink or celebration effects visible.
A few dots on the fairway (possibly aim dots); no dust, sparkle, debris or confetti on a 3-star finish.
Crate tumble implies rigid-body physics; nothing else animates (flags, trees, ball spin cues).
No character, avatar or golfer; the ball is the protagonist and has no personality.
Opening chase cam is serviceable; the wide cam is generic, and neither frames the "siege" fantasy.
Symmetrical corridor with a dead center line; wide shot is ~40% empty plane and the giant blob crowds the goal.
Ellipsoid "trees" are ambiguous in size; no atmospheric perspective, no detail falloff and a flat horizon.
No fog, haze gradient, god rays or sky detail beyond cube clouds.
Lane, ball, target and obstacles read clearly; obstacle color is too close to the goal ring's coral.

Clean system sans with legible hierarchy; generic, with no game-brand voice.
3-star completion with no celebration, no screen effects, nothing shown landing or popping.
Modal plus control bar eat ~45% of the screen; the scene is washed and blurred, with contradictory UI text.
Reads as a competent engine test scene with primitive art, below "dated programmer-art" in authored intent.
One untextured green blob that doesn't span the screen, and in 3 of 4 shots no world at all.
The lander has reasonable silhouette detail (dome, legs, panels, antenna) but is chunky and low-poly. The terrain is a smooth noise mesh.
No visible textures anywhere; everything is flat albedo.
The lander reads as flat teal plastic with no metal/roughness variation. The terrain is matte flat green.
No specular response or Fresnel, and nothing reads as metal, regolith or glass.

No shadows visible: none from the lander on the ground, and no self-shadowing on its legs. (Partly inferred: the ground is rarely on screen.)

No environment reflections on any surface.

Weak bloom halos on the flame and dots only. No grading, vignette, chromatic or lens treatment. The bloom on the stray dot looks like a bug.
The exhaust is a single static additive capsule mesh: no flicker shape, no taper to a nozzle, no shock diamonds, no heat.
No exhaust particles, dust kick-up, RCS puffs or debris. The "stars" are a dozen dots.
Rigid-body tilt only. There is no visible leg suspension, RCS pulse or flame variance cue in the stills.

The camera frames empty sky and loses the ground entirely at altitude. There is no altitude-adaptive zoom and no lead toward the target pad.
The subject floats in a void. The pad is cropped at the corner, and frames have no foreground, midground or background layering.
There are no depth cues (parallax, haze, size reference) and the stars sit in the same visual plane as the lander. 60 m and 120 m look identical.

The HUD numbers are legible, but the core gameplay information (where the ground and pad are, distance and slope) is often absent from the view.
Clean, consistent chip styling and a tidy sidebar. It reads as dev-tool or prototype ("PROTOTYPE · AUTHORED ARCADE DYNAMICS"). The fuel bar is a sliver.
The monospace HUD is legible and on-theme. The sidebar text is tiny at 1080p, and the title has no hierarchy or brand treatment.
No camera shake, flame flicker, screen-space feedback, landing guides or ground glow. The game is static and silent-looking.
The controls are thumb-sized and well spaced. The HUD wraps into three rows, the subject hugs the edge, the panel eats a third of the screen, and the playfield is still mostly empty.
It reads as a functional prototype: early-2000s Flash/tech-demo level art direction on a modern renderer.
Flat untextured planes, one decal, no set dressing, sky, walls, or architecture. Reads as a greybox.
Barricade is a decent stock scan. Everything else is quads, hexagons, and ellipses.
Only the barricade has textures (good, but off-theme). The floor and all other surfaces have none.
Floor is matte flat color, enemies are flat-shaded, and black blobs look like missing materials.
Barricade responds plausibly. Nothing else shows roughness or metal variation, and there is no specular on the floor.
Dim ambient plus a couple of colored point pools. No key/rim and no light shaping the player.
No visible cast/contact shadows on barricades or player. Black ellipses may be blob shadows, but they are opaque and unreadable.
No AO at plane seams or under props. Objects float.
No reflections on what should be a glossy neon floor, and no visible environment map contribution.
No clipping except bloom cores, but blacks are crushed and the midrange is murky.
Palette intent (cyan/magenta) is there. Teal planes look washed and the barricade orange fights the palette.
Edges acceptably clean at 1080p. Thin barricade legs show mild stepping (inferred, JPEG).
Bloom on emissives is tasteful but the only effect visible. No vignette, grading, chromatic aberration, or scanline treatment for a neon theme.
Ring glow and arrow only. No combat VFX despite score changes.
None visible in any frame (inferred absent).
Identical static T-ish pose across three gameplay captures (inferred no locomotion/idle).
Silhouette shape is OK, but it is dark-on-dark, unlit, and has no rim, trail, or personality.
Readable top-down angle for a twin-stick game, but too close/tight, and props get cropped awkwardly at frame edges.
Large dead black regions, random prop placement, no framing of the play space or arena boundaries.
Only the barricade conveys scale. Floor height steps are ambiguous and there are no depth cues.
Faint colored floor pools. No fog, haze, volumetrics, or dust.
Enemies, hazards, and pickups are not distinguishable. "36 drones" with nothing clearly hostile on screen.
Clean, consistent glass panels and legible, but generic dev-dashboard styling and text-heavy.
Neat system sans with a good hierarchy. No display face or theme identity.
No hit feedback, trails, screen shake cues, or reactive lighting visible.
Functional joysticks, but the HUD eats the top quarter and the 3D view is cramped and dark.
Reads as an early prototype/greybox with one marketplace prop dropped in.
Flat solid-color void plus translucent rings; no skybox, nebula or star depth.
Voxel truck, primitive spheres, noisy spire stations; the three asset languages clash.

Everything is unlit, flat or translucent; black spheres have no response at all.
No visible roughness/metal variation, specular or Fresnel anywhere.

None visible. Even planet self-shadowing from the central star is absent.

No environment reflections on the ship or planets.
No blown highlights, but also no HDR; the sun is a flat LDR disc.
Coherent teal/cyan palette, but low contrast and the backdrop and rings blend into mud-teal.

No bloom, vignette, grading or DOF.

Static white dots; no engine trail or ambient dust.
A rigid voxel prop sliding; the detached box suggests broken parenting.

The system is centered, but the rings overlap into visual soup and the right cluster is crowded.

No corona, planet atmospheres or haze.

Cropped canvas, label collisions, half-screen desktop HUD, keyboard hints on touch.

Everything is matte or emissive. No car paint, glass, wet asphalt, or metal response.

Pure emissive-driven night with no motivated key light. The van is lit by its own bloom rather than the scene.
No visible cast shadows from van, barriers, or buildings. Objects float.
Flat navy ambient. No AO or contact darkening, and edges crush to black.

None visible in any frame.

No fog, haze, rain, volumetric light cones, or sky.
